rows.unit: One local orbital model used to predict carbon bonding, rather than independent competency bundles.
rows.source: BY C12-GA.4.5 and HE printed41 specify the hybrid model; HE needs the simplified sp3/sp2/sp and sigma/pi content, not the entire diatomic MO-energy-level sequence.
rows.prerequisites: Simple atomic orbitals, bond types and EPA give the actual starting knowledge. A required whole diatomic MO chain would import extra course content.
rows.P: Methane/ethene/ethyne compare hybrid directions and residual p orbitals; fresh propene forces a separate local assignment, CH3 sp3 and both double-bond carbon atoms sp2. These cases expose actual model use.
rows.M: memory_required: compact sp/sp2/sp3 geometry associations support application; inspected chem_bond_009. The course-matched narrow unit 64d71d34 selects the bond-types card and hybrid card only.
rows.V: Displayed table has 4/3/2 hybrid orbitals, 0/1/2 residual p orbitals, correct tetrahedral/trigonal-planar/linear angles and correct methane/ethene/ethyne sigma/pi counts.

rows.unit: One stereochemical representation competence, including its necessary spatial convention and classification.
rows.source: HE printed40 places asymmetric C, chirality, Fischer, D/L and enantiomers in the shared course column. CIP/R/S is not required by this clause; optical activity/polarimetry is a separate advanced clause.
rows.prerequisites: General molecule representation is enough because the supplied material explicitly teaches the missing spatial/Fischer/DL conventions.
rows.P: Both complete DE/EN cases are soluble: alanine yields L with D mirror; glycine has two H and no D/L pair. The rotated cysteine input becomes L after the permitted180-degree paper turn; new serine is D. The90-degree renewed Fischer reading reverses configuration; physical rotation of a molecule does not interconvert enantiomers. D/L gives no rotation sign. Both12-point rubrics and fresh transfer match the goal.
rows.M: no_memory_needed: the assessed capability is independent spatial translation and explanation; the necessary conventions are supplied. No new separate recall deck is justified by these tasks.
rows.V: Retain the existing image: COOH top, CH3 bottom, NH2 left for L-alanine and right for D-alanine; a vertical mirror correctly relates the two complete projections.

rows.unit: One acyl substitution/condensation model transferred between oxygen and nitrogen nucleophiles.
rows.source: BY C11.3.5 explicitly requires ester and amide condensation mechanism. Neither whole Q1.3 nor digestive fluids is part of this clause.
rows.prerequisites: Existing ester and peptide/amide foundations are relevant; the removed digestive-fluid and broad cluster dependencies are unnecessary for the complete current cases.
rows.P: Read both complete bilingual cases. Products balance atoms. Protonated carbonyl, tetrahedral intermediate, proton transfer, water departure and regenerated acid are correct for the ester model. The amide cases explicitly require activating dehydration; the cold ammonium salt is not treated as an amide and NH4+ is not called a nucleophile. Methanol/ethylamine changes test O-to-N mechanistic transfer.
rows.M: no_memory_needed: mechanistic explanation and transfer use already acquired acyl/ester/amide foundations; memorizing the two product examples would not supply the evidence.
rows.V: The net equations and highlighted eliminated H/OH are correct. The visible note preserves the need for activation or reactive derivatives in practical amidation; the image is a net-reaction aid, not a complete mechanism proof.

rows.unit: One qualitative Faraday-law relationship, with fixed reaction charge, electron demand, amount and mass distinguished.
rows.source: HE printed45 advanced course explicitly says Faraday laws without calculation. This is qualitative HE-LK content. Cross-country use as a prerequisite of quantitative Faraday does not create HE-GK duty.
rows.prerequisites: Electrolysis supplies electron transfer/product identity; molar mass supplies the separate amount/mass relation. Thermodynamic electrolysis potentials and pH preparation are not required to solve these cases.
rows.P: Read both complete bilingual10-point cases. B has more charge and Cu than A; C and A give equal Cu under equal reaction-specific charge. Competing hydrogen explains lower Cu without violating the law. Equal charge gives equal Cu/Ni amount but greater Cu mass for supplied molar-mass order. Ag needs fewer electrons and also has larger molar mass; fresh Zn/Cu distinguishes equal amount from unequal mass. No numerical current/time/charge/mass calculation is requested.
rows.M: memory_required: inspected new cards012/013. They accurately encode the fixed-reaction/efficiency condition, amount versus mass and electron demand. Actual stock filter selects exactly these two cards; new memory03b depends on the learned ordinary goal.
rows.V: Actual source PNG SHA3021201619f84a95ade04354a0a82abdb5e1e9cfcb1a97d9c176db37830bdbdf inspected at native size and actual browser widths360/680. Left upper2 electrons/2 Ag+ yield2 Ag; lower6/6 yield6. Right equal4 electrons yield4 Ag or2 Cu from2 Cu2+. Bottom explicitly separates amount and molar mass. Readable and no numerical values are asserted.

rows.unit: One chemical secretion model used to explain inhibition of the same proton transport.
rows.source: BY C11.3.1 explicitly joins gastric-acid formation with the proton-pump inhibitor.
rows.prerequisites: Digestive-fluid/pH foundation is relevant. The whole Q1.3 cluster is not needed; task material provides ATP-coupled transport and the ideal pH formula.
rows.P: Both full bilingual cases distinguish new H+ secretion from consumption of existing acid. The NCI mechanism supports the stated pump target. Model pH1.921/1.991 and2.222/2.097 agree with supplied ideal amounts/volumes. The result does not imply individual onset, efficacy or treatment selection.
rows.M: no_memory_needed: understanding the causal transport/inhibition relation is assessed; a drug-name or pump-label deck would not replace it.
rows.V: The four stages correctly show CO2/H2O as proton source, apical H+/K+-ATPase, basolateral bicarbonate/chloride exchange and lower new H+ secretion after pump inhibition.

rows.unit: One source-supported chemical appraisal of analgesics; research, structure and data denominators contribute to the same judgment.
rows.source: BY C11.3.4 explicitly includes composition, consumption and application appraisal through chemistry of active molecules. Ester/amide classes are developed in the material; a whole Q1.3/physiology cluster is not a universal prerequisite.
rows.prerequisites: O-containing functional-group recognition and chemical source work support the tasks. No digestive-fluid knowledge or separate COX mastery is needed.
rows.P: Read both complete DE/EN cases. ASS has free acid and ester, ibuprofen acid, paracetamol phenol and amide.600/360/500g and1.2/1.8/1.0 tablets per person are correct. Case2 gives X1.5, Y2.0 tablets/person/30days and150g each X ingredient,320g ibuprofen. Historical RKI measurements remain distinct from fabricated sales, OTC-only scope and current prevalence.2.2 percentage points/22% relative change is correct. IQWiG supports the bounded application distinctions; molecular structure alone does not establish clinical interchangeability.
rows.M: no_memory_needed: the goal calls for interpreting source-supported molecular and consumption information; memorizing labels or sales numbers would be inappropriate.
rows.V: Actual ASS is ortho-substituted with COOH and ring-O-C(=O)-CH3, labeled acid and ester. The equal balance treats benefit/risk as the two sides and source work as evidence, without a clinical recommendation.

rows.unit: One evidence-based chemical comparison of digestive aids using substrate, interface and microbial mechanisms.
rows.source: BY C11.3.3 includes the four aid groups. This does not introduce all Q1.3 organic content as prior knowledge.
rows.prerequisites: Enzymes, individual digestion, digestive fluids and criteria-based evaluation are retained and relevant; source dossiers and substrate formulas supply the case-specific information.
rows.P: Read both complete DE/EN cases. Lactose hydrolysis yields equal glucose/galactose;8mmol conversion leaves2mmol. Full0.60mmol triacylglycerol hydrolysis yields0.60mmol glycerol and1.80mmol acids;40-to12mm foam is70% decrease. NIDDK, ODS and product SmPC have distinct evidence roles. Simeticone is not lipase; neither foam nor fabricated conversions are clinical benefit evidence.
rows.M: no_memory_needed: the required evidence is an explained comparison and source judgment, with mechanisms in supplied material. A parallel four-group recall deck is unnecessary.
rows.V: Table correctly separates substrate-specific enzymes, physical defoaming, fermentable prebiotic substrate and live probiotic strains. It limits general efficacy and makes dose/strain/indication dependence visible.
